ga-grammar-01: Blank ke baad ka clue dekho: 'voted it down without even discussing it' — rejection kaisa tha? Jaldi aur bina kisi process ke.
Aisa word chahiye jiska matlab ho 'turant, bina formalities ke'. Charon options ka meaning likho: tentatively, sumptuously, subsequently, summarily.
*Tentatively* = jhijhakte hue — yeh 'bina discussion ke turant reject' se match nahi karta, cut. Trap: sound-alike se bacho; *sumptuously* ka matlab 'lavishly / mehenga' hai.
ga-grammar-02: Article spelling se nahi, word ki pehli **sound** se decide hota hai. 'honest' aur 'useful' dono ko zor se bol ke dekho.
Rule: vowel sound → *an*, consonant sound → *a*. Pehli letter h ya u dekh ke decide mat karo, sirf awaaz suno.
'useful' bolo: 'yoo-sful' — shuru 'y' (consonant) sound se hota hai, toh doosre blank ka article tay. Ab 'honest' mein h bolte ho ya silent hai, khud check karo.
ga-grammar-03: 'By next March' future ka ek point hai, aur 'six years' ek duration hai — dono blanks inhi do clues se decide honge.
Rule: 'by + future time' → future perfect (*will have + V3*). Aur *for* + duration, *since* + starting point (jaise since 2020).
Pehle socho: 'six years' starting point hai ya length of time? Uske hisaab se since/for chuno. Trap: 'has worked' (present perfect) sirf 'ab tak' batata hai, future deadline nahi.
ga-grammar-04: Teen confusable words: assure, ensure, insure. Har blank ke baad dekho kya aata hai — ek person (the inspectors), ek outcome (power), ya property against damage.
Rule: *assure* + person (kisi ko bharosa dilana); *ensure* + outcome (pakka karna); *insure* + property against risk (financial cover).
Blank 1 ke baad 'the inspectors' hai — person, toh wahi verb chahiye jo person ko object leta hai. Baaki do blanks khud match karo; trap: ensure aur insure swap mat karna.
ga-grammar-05: Pehle Cartographer aur Map ka relation ek sentence mein bolo — cartographer map ke saath kya karta hai? Order yaad rakho: pehle person, phir cheez.
Relation: 'A cartographer **makes** a map' (maker : thing made). Ab har pair ko isi sentence mein, isi order mein daal ke test karo.
Painter : Brush — 'A painter makes a brush'? Nahi, brush toh tool hai, cut. Trap: sahi relation par ulta order (thing : maker) bhi galat hai.
ga-grammar-06: Drought aur Famine ka relation bolo: drought se kya hota hai? Yeh cause → effect pair hai, aur order mein cause pehle hai.
Test sentence: 'X causes Y' — pehla word cause, doosra effect. Har option ko isi order mein bol ke dekho.
Flood : Rain — 'Flood causes rain'? Nahi, rain flood ka cause hai, yani order ulta, cut. Trap: sirf related hona kaafi nahi — measuring tool (thermometer) ya remedy (food) cause-effect nahi hai.
ga-grammar-07: Clue: 'but journalists soon uncovered the full story' — *but* contrast dikhata hai, matlab company ne kuch chhupane ki koshish ki thi.
Aisa phrasal verb chahiye jiska matlab ho 'kisi event ya galti ko chhupana'. Har option ka meaning likho: cover for, play up, make up, cover up.
*Play up* = exaggerate, yani badha-chadha ke batana — chhupane ka ulta, cut. Trap: *cover for* kisi person ko bachane ya uski jagah kaam karne ke liye hota hai, event hide karne ke liye nahi.
ga-grammar-08: Dono blanks ke aas-paas ke words dekho: pehla 'a strong ___' ke baad hai, doosra 'did not ___' ke baad. Ek jagah noun chahiye, ek jagah verb.
Rule: *effect* normally noun hai (result), *affect* normally verb hai (influence karna). Article + adjective ke baad noun aata hai; 'did not' ke baad verb.
'a strong ___' — 'a' aur 'strong' ke baad noun chahiye, toh pehla blank noun wala word. Ab 'did not ___' ke liye khud decide karo; trap: *effect* as a verb ka matlab 'bring about' hota hai.
ga-grammar-09: Har option mein subject–verb agreement test ho raha hai. Har sentence ka asli subject dhoondo — beech ke 'of the reports' jaise phrase se dhokha mat khao.
Rules: *a number of* → plural verb; *the number of* → singular; *each of* → singular; *neither A nor B* → verb B (nearer subject) se match karega.
'Each of the reports have been reviewed': subject *Each* hai (singular), toh 'have' theek nahi, cut. Baaki teen options par yahi rules ek-ek karke lagao.
ga-grammar-10: Question **opposite** maang raha hai, synonym nahi. Pehle *ephemeral* ka meaning yaad karo — yeh time / duration ke baare mein hai.
*ephemeral* = bahut kam time tak rehne wala (short-lived). Opposite = lambe time tak rehne wala. Har option ka meaning likho.
*fleeting* ka matlab bhi short-lived hai — yeh synonym hai, opposite nahi, cut. Trap: *ethereal* sound mein milta-julta hai par matlab 'delicate / heavenly' hai.
ga-grammar-11: *Although* contrast dikhata hai: pehla blank 'praised' se juda hai, doosra 'gave up halfway' se. Dono blanks opposite direction mein honge.
Blank 1 = positive word (praise kiya), blank 2 = negative word (beech mein chhod di). Har option ke dono words ki polarity (+ / −) likho.
'lucid; engrossing': lucid (clear) positive theek, par engrossing (bahut interesting) book koi beech mein nahi chhodta, cut. Trap: sirf ek blank fit dekh ke option mat chuno — dono fit hone chahiye.
ga-grammar-12: Teeno blanks (hour, European, MBA) ka article first letter se nahi, pehli **sound** se decide hoga. Har word ko zor se bolo.
Rule: vowel sound → *an*, consonant sound → *a*. Abbreviation (MBA) letter-by-letter bola jaata hai, toh pehli letter ke **naam** ki sound dekho.
'hour' bolo: h silent hai, vowel sound se shuru, toh pehla blank tay. Ab European aur MBA bol ke unki pehli sound khud check karo; trap: E ya M letter dekh ke decide mat karna.
ga-reading-01: Question 'best supported' maang raha hai. Passage ka 'however' wala sentence dhyan se padho: 'The streets, however, were not randomly selected…'.
Rule: agar streets random nahi chuni gayi aur speeds pehle se gir rahi thi, toh poora credit lanes ko dena risky hai. Har option ko is sentence se match karo.

'Speed checks explain the 30% fall' ko last sentence se check karo: checks **whole city** mein the, par baaki streets par injuries unchanged rahi — kya ye farak explain kar sakte hain? Trap: 'not randomly' ko 'randomly' padhna.
ga-reading-02: Question mein **beyond** hai — tumhe wo statement chahiye jo passage support NAHI karta. Teen options passage mein seedhe mil jayenge.
Har option ke saamne likho: stated / inferable / passage mein hai hi nahi. Sirf 'hai hi nahi' wala chahiye.

'Evaporating water is used to cool the hive' — second sentence ('spread it on the comb… evaporation cools the air') mein stated hai, toh beyond nahi. Trap: supported option chun lena, jabki question ulta hai.
ga-reading-03: Yeh direction of influence ka question hai: crabs birds ko affect karte hain ya birds crabs ko? Do experiment wale sentences ('crabs were removed', 'birds were kept out') dobara padho.
Logic: agar X hatane se Y badalta hai par Y hatane se X nahi badalta, toh influence X → Y hai. Dono experiments mein dekho kya badla.

Fenced plots (birds bahar) mein crab numbers 'no measurable change' — toh 'birds control crabs' wala option iske against jaata hai. Trap: 'main food during the breeding season' ko 'only food all year' mat bana dena.
ga-reading-04: Main idea = wo claim jise poora passage support karta hai, koi ek detail nahi. Last sentence ('The result is a system in which…') dhyan se padho.
Har option ko classify karo: supporting detail / passage se bahar / passage ke against / poore passage ka summary. Main idea sirf last type hoga.

'Some large firms pay staff…' — passage mein hai, par sirf ek detail hai, poore passage ka point nahi. Trap: 'These efforts remain small…' padho — kisi option ne problem ko 'solved' toh nahi bata diya?
ga-reading-05: Passage mein **do** changes hain: closing 6 pm se 9 pm, aur opening 9 am se noon. Question sirf evening (closing) wale change ka reason pooch raha hai.
'Instead, a survey showed…' wala sentence ek change ka reason deta hai, aur 'because morning visits…' wala doosre ka. Dono reasons alag-alag likho.
'Morning visits had been the lowest' — yeh kis change ka reason hai, later opening ka ya later closing ka? Trap: 'costs unchanged' ko 'reduced' aur 'flat' visitors ko 'rising' mat padhna.
ga-reading-06: Question mein **NOT** hai — options padhne se pehle ise circle karo. Tumhe wo statement chahiye jo passage support nahi karta.
Har option ko passage ki ek line se match karo. Last sentence ('The plant's engineers caution, however…') khaas dhyan se padho — wo output gain ke baare mein kya kehta hai?
'Dust on panels can reduce their output' — first sentence mein stated hai, toh supported hai, NOT question mein yeh nahi chalega. Trap: 'sahi lagne wala' supported option chun lena.
ga-reading-07: 'Most justified' conclusion chahiye. Do phrases dekho: 'Patients chose their routine themselves' aur 'Because the groups were not randomised…'.
Rule: jab groups khud chune gaye aur unme pehle se farak hai (younger, fitter), toh recovery ka farak sirf routine ki wajah se hai, yeh claim nahi kar sakte — sirf association dikhta hai.

'The hospital has already switched its guidelines' check karo: authors trial recommend karte hain **before** any change, toh yeh passage ke against hai. Trap: 'not randomised' ko 'randomly assigned' padh lena.
ga-reading-08: Question sirf 'only in classrooms' wale programmes ke outcome ke baare mein hai. Passage ka last sentence ('Programmes that teach a language only in classrooms…') dobara padho.
Passage do tarah ke programmes ke outcomes batata hai: school + home/community wale, aur classroom-only wale. Option ko sahi type ke programme se match karo.
'better job prospects' wala option dekho — passage mein jobs ka zikr kyon aaya: language decline ka cause ya revival ka result? Trap: 'seldom speak' ko 'no speakers at all' tak exaggerate mat karna.
ga-reading-09: 'Must hold' = necessary condition, sirf ek example nahi. Sales team kehti hai total revenue badhega, jabki price 20% kam ho raha hai.
Revenue = price × quantity. Naya price $=0.8\times$ purana; quantity factor $q$ maano. Revenue badhne ke liye $0.8\,q > 1$ chahiye.
Pehle 20% rise test karo: $0.8 \times 1.2 = 0.96 < 1$, revenue abhi bhi girta hai. Ab $0.8q>1$ ko $q$ ke liye solve karo; trap: rival ka 'double' sufficient hai, necessary nahi.
ga-reading-10: Question mein **beyond** hai — study ki limit dhoondo. Last sentence ('The study covered only engineers and designers…') dhyan se padho.
Har option ke liye check karo: kya yeh study wale logon (engineers, designers) ke baare mein hai aur passage mein stated hai? Jo study ke scope se bahar jaye, wohi beyond hai.

'Managers' views changed' — passage kehta hai unhone output girne ki ummeed ki thi par end mein kaha performance hurt nahi hui; toh supported hai. Trap: supported statement chun lena, kyunki question ulta hai.
ga-reading-11: Question curators ke view ka **before → after** change pooch raha hai. Wo sentence dhoondo jisme 'had long regarded the storerooms as…' aur 'began to see them as…' hai.
Pehla view (shuru mein storerooms unke liye kya the) aur baad wala view alag-alag likho; phir last sentence (permanent gallery plan) se confirm karo.

'They had expected long queues from the start' — pehla sentence 'modest interest' kehta hai, toh yeh contradict karta hai. Trap: 'unlabelled tools' padho — kisi option ne ulta 'labelled' toh nahi bola?
ga-numerical-01: Question **total students** pooch raha hai, sirf boys nahi. Ratio 5 : 7 mein girls ke 7 parts = 21.
Ek part = girls ÷ 7. Total = (5 + 7) parts × ek part.
Ek part $= 21/7 = 3$. Ab total parts se multiply karo; trap: sirf boys (5 parts) nikaal ke ruk mat jaana.
ga-numerical-02: Pani add karne se milk **change nahi hota** — sirf water aur total badalte hain. Toh pehle 60 L mein milk aur water alag nikalo.
Milk $= \frac{7}{10}\times 60$, water $= \frac{3}{10}\times 60$. Naya water $w$ ho toh milk : $w$ = 3 : 2.
Milk $=42$ L, water $=18$ L. Ab $42/w = 3/2$ se $w$ nikalo, phir usme se 18 ghatao; trap: final water ko hi 'added' mat bolna, aur total 60 fixed mat maanna.
ga-numerical-03: Kisi number ke digits uske $\log_{10}$ se nikalte hain. Yahan $2^{50}$ hai aur $\log_{10}2 = 0.301$ diya hai.
$50 \times 0.301 = 15.05$. Ab formula lagao; trap: integer part (15) ko hi digit count mat maan lena — $10^{15}$ khud kitne digits ka hai, socho.
ga-numerical-04: Teen alag logs hain, har ek alag se nikalo: $\log_2 8$, $\log_3 \frac19$, $\log_5 1$. Har ek ke liye socho: base ko kitni power dene se yeh number milta hai?
Rule: $\log_b b^k = k$. Toh $8 = 2^{?}$, $\frac19 = 3^{?}$ (fraction hai, toh power negative hogi), aur kisi bhi base mein $\log 1 = 0$.
$\log_2 8 = 3$ kyunki $2^3 = 8$. Ab $\frac19$ ko 3 ki power mein likh ke doosra term nikalo aur signs dhyan se jodo; trap: $\log_3\frac19$ ka minus sign gira dena.
ga-numerical-05: Terms 3, 7, 15, 31, 63 tezi se badh rahe hain — har term pichhle ka lagbhag double hai. Pehle consecutive differences nikalo.
Differences: $7-3,\ 15-7,\ 31-15,\ 63-31$. Dekho ye kis pattern mein badh rahe hain — ya check karo kya term $= 2\times$ previous $+1$ hai.
Differences 4, 8, 16, 32 hain — har baar double. Agla difference nikaal ke 63 mein jodo; trap: last difference 32 repeat mat karna, aur $2\times63$ ke baad $+1$ mat bhoolna.
ga-numerical-06: Average se seedha number nahi milta — pehle **sums** nikalo. 5 numbers ka average 18, aur ek hatane ke baad 4 ka average 16.
Sum = average × count. Removed number = (5 numbers ka sum) − (4 numbers ka sum) $= 5\times18 - 4\times16$.
5 numbers ka sum $= 5\times 18 = 90$. Ab 4 numbers ka sum nikaal ke ghatao; trap: average ka drop (2) ko hi removed number mat samajhna.
ga-numerical-07: Days directly add/subtract nahi hote, **rates** (kaam per day) add hote hain. A ka rate $\frac1{12}$, B ka $\frac1{18}$ job per day.
4 din saath: kaam $= 4\left(\frac1{12}+\frac1{18}\right)$. Bacha kaam $= 1 -$ ye. B ke din $=$ bacha kaam ÷ $\frac1{18}$.
$\frac1{12}+\frac1{18} = \frac{3+2}{36} = \frac5{36}$, toh 4 din mein $\frac{20}{36}$ kaam hua. Ab bacha kaam aur B ke din nikalo; trap: pehle 4 din mein B ka kaam bhool jaana.
ga-numerical-08: Do dice ke outcomes **ordered pairs** hote hain — (2,6) aur (6,2) alag hain. Total outcomes kitne hain, aur sum 8 kaun se pairs dete hain?
P = (sum 8 wale ordered pairs) / 36. List banao: first die 1 se 6 tak, second $= 8 -$ first, jab tak woh 1–6 ke andar ho.
First die 1 ho toh second 7 chahiye — impossible. First 2 ho toh (2,6) chalega. Aise baaki values check karo; trap: sums 2–12 ko equally likely maanna, ya (3,5) aur (5,3) ko ek hi ginna.
ga-numerical-09: 'Closest to' — exact calculation ki zaroorat nahi. Har number ko easy value ke paas round karo: 49.8, 0.0198, 0.251.
Numerator: $50\times0.02 = 1$. Ab 0.25 se **divide** karo (multiply nahi); trap: decimal khisak jaana — 0.0198 ko 0.198 mat padhna.
ga-numerical-10: Teen layers hain: list ke voters → jinhone vote diya (90%) → valid votes (cast − 60). Margin 120 **valid** votes par hai — wahan se peeche ki taraf chalo.
Winner 52%, loser 48% of valid, toh margin $= 4\%$ of valid $= 120$. Phir cast $=$ valid $+ 60$, aur cast $= 0.9 \times$ list.
$0.04 \times V = 120$ se valid votes $V$ nikalo, phir 60 jodo, phir 0.9 wala step. Trap: votes cast ya valid votes par ruk jaana — question **list** ke voters pooch raha hai.
ga-numerical-11: 'Compounded' hai — har saal 10% badhe hue size par lagta hai, toh simple 10 × 10% wala logic nahi chalega. Smallest full $n$ chahiye jahan size double se zyada ho.
Condition: $1.1^n > 2$. Powers of 1.1 ek-ek karke compute karo, ya $n > \frac{\log 2}{\log 1.1}$ nikaal ke next integer lo.
$1.1^2 = 1.21$, $1.1^4 = 1.21^2 \approx 1.4641$. Ab aage 1.1 se multiply karte raho jab tak 2 cross na ho; trap: rule of 72 ka 7.2 round down kar dena — exact check karo.
ga-numerical-12: Do solutions mix ho rahe hain: unknown $x$ L of 30% aur 20 L of 70%, result 40%. Acid ki total quantity dono taraf barabar honi chahiye.
Acid balance: $0.3x + 0.7\times 20 = 0.4(x+20)$. Ya alligation: weak : strong $= (70-40) : (40-30)$.
Alligation ratio $30 : 10 = 3 : 1$ (weak : strong), aur strong 20 L hai. Ab weak ki quantity nikalo; trap: total mixture report kar dena, ya ratio ulta (1 : 3) laga dena.
ga-di-01: Chart se sirf Q3 aur Q4 ki values padho (Q1, Q2 nahi). Percentage change mein base hamesha **purani** value hoti hai.
% rise $= \frac{Q4 - Q3}{Q3}\times100$. Chart se Q3 = 45, Q4 = 60.
Change $= 60-45 = 15$ crore. Ab ise base 45 se divide karo; trap: 15 crore ko hi 15% bol dena, ya nayi value 60 se divide kar dena.
ga-di-02: Question **share** pooch raha hai: (May + June) ÷ (chhe mahine ka total). Chart se har mahine ki value padho.
May + June $= 120 + 95 = 215$. Ab chhe values jod ke actual total nikalo aur divide karo; trap: total ko 600 (6 × 100) maan lena.
ga-di-03: Sections ke size alag hain (30, 50, 20), toh teen averages ka seedha average nahi chalega — **weighted** average chahiye.
Overall avg $= \frac{30\cdot62 + 50\cdot78 + 20\cdot66}{100}$. Har section ka total score = students × average.
Section A ka total $= 30\times62 = 1860$. B aur C ke totals nikaal ke jodo, phir 100 se divide karo; trap: $(62+78+66)/3$ wala plain average, ya weights galat rows se jodna.
ga-di-04: Question **profit** ka % increase pooch raha hai, revenue ya cost ka nahi. Pehle dono saal ka profit nikalo.
Profit 2023 $= 250-200 = 50$ lakh. Ab 2024 ka profit nikaal ke formula lagao; trap: revenue growth (250 → 300) ko profit growth samajh lena.
ga-di-05: 'Python exceeds DBMS by what %' — comparison DBMS **se** ho raha hai, toh base DBMS hai. Chart se dono bars ki values padho.
Difference $= 50 - 25 = 25$ students. Ab base se divide karo; trap: '% of' (Python ÷ DBMS) aur '% more' (difference ÷ DBMS) ko mix kar dena.
ga-di-06: Teen plants ki growth compare karni hai — absolute rise nahi, **percentage** growth. Har plant ke liye base January ki value hogi.
P: rise $= 18$, base 60 → $18/60$. Q aur R ke liye bhi same karo (base January hi) aur har option check karo; trap: R ka absolute rise sabse bada hai, par % alag cheez hai.
ga-di-07: Average se seedha Saturday nahi milta — **sums** mein socho. Chart se Mon–Fri ki paanch values padho: 1200, 1500, 900, 1800, 1600.
Mon–Fri total $= 1200+1500+900+1800+1600 = 7000$. Ab $6\times1450$ nikaal ke ghatao; trap: naye din ko naye average (1450) ke barabar maan lena.
ga-di-08: Rent **rupees mein fixed** hai, sirf income badh rahi hai — toh rent ka share girega. Table ke baaki items (food, savings…) is question mein kaam nahi aayenge.
Rent $= 30\%$ of ₹60,000. New income $= 1.1\times60{,}000$. New share $= \frac{\text{rent}}{\text{new income}}\times100$.
Rent $= 0.30\times60{,}000 = ₹18{,}000$. Ab nayi income nikaal ke divide karo; trap: share ko seedha 10 points kam (30 → 20) kar dena.
ga-di-09: Highest **percentage** increase chahiye, absolute nahi. Legend se pehchaano: light bar = 2023, dark bar = 2024, aur har product ki dono values padho.
A: $(50-40)/40 = 10/40$. Baaki teen ke liye bhi 2023 ko base rakh ke nikalo; trap: B mein bars ka farak bada dikhta hai, par 2024 wala chhota hai — woh decrease hai.
ga-di-10: Har grade ki quantity alag hai (40, 25, 35 kg), toh teen prices ka seedha average nahi chalega — quantity se **weighted** average chahiye.
Regular ka revenue $= 40\times50 = ₹2000$. Premium aur Basmati ka nikaal ke jodo, phir total kg se divide karo; trap: $(50+60+80)/3$ plain average, ya quantity ko galat price se jodna.
ga-di-11: Sirf Sales mein hiring ho rahi hai, toh Engineering (120) fixed rahega. Question **poori firm ka total** pooch raha hai, sirf Sales nahi.
Eng : Sales $= 5 : 4$ with Eng $=120$ → new Sales $= 120\times\frac45$. Hires $=$ new Sales − 80. New total $=$ current total + hires.
Current total $= 120+80+60+40 = 300$. Ab naya Sales count aur hires nikaal ke total update karo; trap: naye Sales count ya hires ki sankhya par hi ruk jaana.
ga-reasoning-01: 'Unless' wala rule: 'The server will not restart unless the administrator approves.' Pehle ise if-then mein badlo — phir sirf contrapositive hi pakka follow karta hai.
Rule: 'not P unless Q' = 'if not Q then not P'. Iska contrapositive: P → Q. Converse aur inverse follow nahi karte.
Yahan P = restart, Q = approve, toh rule: 'no approval → no restart'. Har option ko if-then mein likho aur pehchaano — contrapositive kaunsa hai? Trap: approval *necessary* hai, *sufficient* nahi.
ga-reasoning-02: 'Unless it rains, the match will be played' ko if-then mein badlo, phir dekho 'match **not** played' rule ke kis hisse ko negate karta hai.
Rule: 'A unless B' = 'if not B then A'. Yahan A = match played, B = it rains. Phir contrapositive lo: if not A then ___.
If-then: 'no rain → played'. Diya hai 'not played' — consequent ka negation, toh contrapositive antecedent ka negation dega; woh khud likho. Trap: 'rain → cancelled' inverse hai, follow nahi karta.
ga-reasoning-03: Do statements: analysts poore graduates ke andar hain; managers graduates ke saath sirf **kahin** overlap karte hain. Venn diagram banao.
Rule: conclusion tabhi follows jab har possible diagram mein true ho. Aur 'Some A are B' se hamesha 'Some B are A' milta hai (conversion).

Conclusion I test karo: aisa diagram banao jisme managers graduates ko overlap karein par analysts wale circle ko na chhuein — possible hai? Phir II par conversion rule lagao; trap: possible ko certain maan lena.
ga-reasoning-04: 'No sensor is cheap' — sensors aur cheap circles bilkul alag (disjoint). 'Some devices are sensors' — devices sensors ko kahin overlap karte hain. Diagram banao.
Rule: jo conclusion har possible diagram mein true ho, wahi follows. Devices ka jo hissa sensors ke andar hai, uske baare mein cheap ke hisaab se kya pakka hai?
Ab devices ka baaki hissa (sensors ke bahar) — kya woh cheap circle mein ja sakta hai? Ek diagram try karo, isse II test hoga; trap: 'some devices' ko 'all devices' bana dena.
ga-reasoning-05: Paanch seats left se right 1–5 (sab north face kar rahe hain, toh left/right normal hai). Pehle fixed clues lagao: C middle, E right end.
C = seat 3, E = seat 5, aur 'A immediately left of C' → A = seat 2. Bachi seats 1 aur 4, B aur D ke liye.
Ab 'B is not next to E' lagao: seat 5 ke bagal mein kaunsi seat hai? Usse B aur D place karo, phir right se doosri seat dekho; trap: left se count kar lena.
ga-reasoning-06: Saare comparisons ek hi chain mein jodo. Pehla sentence do comparisons deta hai: 'P more than Q' aur 'P less than R'.
Chain: R > P > Q. Ab 'S less than Q' aur 'T more than R' ko is chain ke sahi end par jodo.
S ko Q ke neeche lagao: R > P > Q > S. Ab T ko place karo aur upar se teesra gino; trap: kisi clause ko ulta padhna (jaise Q ko P ke upar rakhna).
ga-reasoning-07: 1, 2, 6, 24, 120 bahut tezi se badh rahe hain — differences ke bajaye consecutive **ratios** dekho.
Ratios: $2/1,\ 6/2,\ 24/6,\ 120/24$. Inka pattern pehchaano (ya socho: kya ye factorials $n!$ hain?).
Ratios 2, 3, 4, 5 hain — multiplier har baar 1 badhta hai. Agla multiplier socho aur 120 se multiply karo; trap: last multiplier ×5 repeat kar dena.
ga-reasoning-08: Letters ko alphabet positions mein badlo (A = 1, …, Z = 26): B, E, I, N, T. Phir gaps dekho.
Positions: 2, 5, 9, 14, 20. Gaps ka pattern nikalo; agar result 26 se upar jaaye toh 26 ghata ke wrap around karo.
Gaps 3, 4, 5, 6 hain — har baar +1. Agla gap 20 mein jodo aur zaroorat ho toh wrap karo; trap: wrap karte waqt off-by-one (A = 1 hai, 0 nahi).
ga-reasoning-09: Data sufficiency: har statement ko pehle **akele** test karo — kya woh integer $x$ ki ek hi value deta hai? Phir zaroorat ho toh dono saath.
I: $x^2 = 16$ ke kitne integer solutions hain? II: $x > 0$ kitni values allow karta hai? Sirf unique value = sufficient.
I se $x = 4$ ya $x = -4$ — do values, toh I akela unique nahi. Ab II akela, aur phir dono saath check karo; trap: negative root bhool jaana.
ga-reasoning-10: Question yes/no hai: 'Is $x > y$?' Statement sufficient tab hai jab woh hamesha ek hi pakka result de — hamesha yes ya hamesha no.
I: $x - y = 5$ ka sign $x$ aur $y$ ke order ke baare mein kya batata hai? II: squares compare karne se order pata chalta hai ya nahi — negative numbers bhi try karo.
II test karo: $x=-3,\ y=1$ lo — $x^2 = 9 > 1 = y^2$, par $x < y$; jabki $x=3,\ y=1$ mein $x>y$. Ab I ko akele check karo; trap: squaring order preserve karta hai, yeh maan lena.
ga-reasoning-11: Path ki total length nahi, start se **displacement** (seedhi doori + direction) chahiye. Har turn ke baad direction track karo — north face karke 'right' = east.
Coordinates lo: start $(0,0)$, north $= +y$, east $= +x$. 5 km north, right (east) 3 km, phir right again (south) 9 km. Distance $= \sqrt{x^2+y^2}$.
Do legs ke baad position $(3, 5)$. Ab 9 km south chalo — naya y kya hoga, aur end point start se kis direction mein hai? Trap: 5 + 3 + 9 jod dena.
ga-spatial-01: Pehle har region ke boundary-sharing neighbours list karo. Dekho: F (centre square) baaki paanchon ko chhoota hai, aur A, B, C, D, E bahar ek ring banate hain.
Rule: ring ko alternate 2 colours se tabhi rang sakte ho jab ring mein regions **even** hon; odd ring ko 3 chahiye. Jo region sabko chhoye, use unse alag naya colour chahiye.
Ring ki adjacencies: A–B, B–C, C–D, D–E, E–A — yeh ring kitne regions ki hai, odd ya even? Uske colours gino, phir F ka effect jodo; trap: ring ko 2 colours se alternate kar dena.
ga-spatial-02: Adjacencies list karo: P, Q, R, S bahar ek ring mein hain aur beech ka circle T sabko chhoota hai. Socho: diagonal pairs (P–R, Q–S) kya koi boundary line share karte hain?
Rule: even ring → 2 alternating colours; odd ring → 3. Jo region sabko chhoye, use ek extra alag colour chahiye.
P aur R ke beech circle T aa jaata hai, toh woh boundary share nahi karte (Q, S bhi nahi). Ab ring ke colours gino aur T ke liye socho; trap: T ko bhool jaana.
ga-spatial-03: Net mein seedhi lines dekho: A, C, E, F upar se neeche ek column mein hain; B, C, D ek row mein. Edge se jude squares fold hone par hamesha adjacent bante hain.
Rule: ek straight line of squares mein alternate squares **opposite** hote hain (ek square chhod ke agla).
Row B, C, D par rule lagao: C beech mein hai, toh B aur D opposite. Ab yahi column A, C, E, F mein A ke liye karo; trap: sabse door wala square automatically opposite nahi hota.
ga-spatial-04: Dono views mein 1 **top** par hai — toh 2, 3, 6 sab 1 ke charon taraf wali side faces ki ring mein hain. Die standard nahi hai, toh 'opposite faces add to 7' mat lagao.
Top fixed ho toh side faces ek ring banate hain: front ke baad right. View 1: front 2, right 3. View 2: front 3, right 6. Ring mein do step door wale faces opposite hote hain.
View 1: ring mein 2 ke baad 3. View 2: 3 ke baad kya? Ring ka order likho aur 2 se do step aage gino; trap: kabhi na dikhe face (4 ya 5) ko opposite maan lena.
ga-spatial-05: Do folds hue (left-onto-right, phir top-down), toh folded piece mein **4 layers** hain — ek punch se unfold par kitne holes? Har unfold ek reflection hai, slide nahi.
Folded piece = sheet ka bottom-right quarter; hole $(80, 70)$ par (100 × 100 sheet, y neeche badhta hai). Ulte order mein kholo: pehle top fold (crease $y = 50$), phir left fold (crease $x = 50$).

Top fold kholo: $(80,70)$ ko crease $y=50$ mein reflect karo — same doori 20 upar, yani $(80,30)$. Ab left fold kholo, dono holes ko $x=50$ mein reflect karo; trap: hole ko crease ke paar slide karna.
ga-spatial-06: Ek hi fold hai, diagonal ke along — toh unfold par 2 holes: original aur uska **reflection** across woh diagonal. Dhyan do kaunsa diagonal hai: top-left se bottom-right.
Sheet 100 × 100, top-left $(0,0)$, x right, y neeche. Crease line $y = x$ hai aur punch $(70, 20)$ par hai. Line $y=x$ mein reflection $x$ aur $y$ ko swap karta hai.
Rule $(a, b) \to (b, a)$ ko punch point par lagao aur dekho naya hole kis corner ki taraf aata hai; trap: 180° rotation, ya vertical/horizontal centre line mein reflect kar dena.
ga-spatial-07: Ek distinctive cell track karo — jaise top row ka right-most shaded cell (top-right corner). 90° **clockwise** mein top row right column ban jaati hai.
3 × 3 grid mein (column $x$, row $y$, dono 0 se 2) clockwise 90° rule: $(x, y) \to (2-y,\ x)$. Rotation rows aur columns ko swap karta hai; mirror nahi karta.

Top-right cell $(2,0) \to (2,2)$, yani bottom-right corner. Ab column 1 wali lambi vertical stem kahan jaayegi, rule se khud nikalo; trap: anticlockwise ghuma dena (top row left column mein chali jaati hai).
ga-spatial-08: Mirror **vertical** hai (figure ke right mein), toh sirf left ↔ right badlega; upar-neeche wahi rahega. Shape ki left column aur bottom row dekho.
Rule: vertical mirror mein $(x, y) \to (2 - x,\ y)$ — har row apni jagah rehti hai, bas ulti ho jaati hai. Mirror kabhi rows ko columns mein nahi badalta.
Top row: shaded cells columns 0 aur 1 mein hain → mirror ke baad columns 2 aur 1 mein. Baaki rows bhi aise hi flip karo; trap: top-bottom flip kar dena (woh water image hai).
ga-spatial-09: Figure mein apex se 4 lines neeche jaati hain (2 sides + 2 andar wali), aur 2 horizontal lines hain (beech wali aur base). Dhyan do: har triangle apex use karta hai.
Ek triangle = apex se nikli koi 2 lines + ek horizontal line base ke roop mein. Ek horizontal line ke liye triangles $= \binom{4}{2}$.
$\binom{4}{2} = 6$ triangles ek horizontal line par. Ab socho kitni horizontal lines base ban sakti hain; trap: sirf chhote triangles, ya ek hi base ke triangles gin ke ruk jaana.
ga-spatial-10: Sirf **squares** chahiye, rectangles nahi — aur har size ke: 1 × 1, 2 × 2, 3 × 3. Grid 4 columns × 3 rows ka hai, toh 4 × 4 square possible nahi.
$m\times n$ grid mein $k\times k$ squares $= (m-k+1)(n-k+1)$. Yahan $m=4,\ n=3$, aur $k = 1, 2, 3$.
$k=1$: $4\times3 = 12$ unit squares. Ab $k=2$ aur $k=3$ ke liye formula lagao aur jodo; trap: $\binom52\times\binom42$ wala rectangles count le lena.
ga-spatial-11: Ek corner chuno; usse edges se jude teen corners se plane guzarta hai. Cut face ki har side in teen mein se do corners ko jodti hai — yeh line cube par kahan padti hai?
Ek corner ke koi do neighbours ek hi face par hote hain, aur unhe jodne wali line us face ka **diagonal** hai. Cube ke saare face diagonals barabar hote hain ($a\sqrt2$).

Corner $(0,0,0)$ lo; neighbours $(1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1)$. Pehle do ke beech doori $= \sqrt{1+1} = \sqrt2$. Baaki do sides nikaal ke shape decide karo; trap: corner ka right angle cut face par carry kar dena.
ga-spatial-12: Cut **tilted** hai aur sirf curved surface ko kaatta hai, flat ends ko nahi — toh cut face ek band (closed) curve hogi.
Rule: axis ke perpendicular cut → circle; axis ke parallel (dono ends tak) → rectangle. Tilted cut circle ko ek direction mein stretch karta hai.

Socho perpendicular cut se tilt badhane par circle ka kya hota hai — ek direction mein lamba, doosri mein wahi diameter. Trap: parabola open curve hai (cone se banti hai), closed cut kabhi open nahi hota.
ga-spatial-13: Pehle khaali region (?) ke cells gino aur uski shape banao: right column ke neeche wale teen cells aur unke bagal ka ek cell. Area 4 cells hai.
Rule: piece rotate kar sakte ho, **flip nahi**. Same area kaafi nahi — shape match honi chahiye: teen cells seedhi line mein + ek cell line ke **end** par, ek khaas side mein.

Gap: right column mein rows 2–4 (khadi bar of 3) aur bottom cell ke left mein ek extra. Har option ko 90° steps mein ghuma ke yahi shape dhoondo; trap: mirror-image piece, jo sirf flip karke fit hota.
ga-spatial-14: Question **NOT** pooch raha hai — wo arrangement dhoondo jo cube nahi ban sakta. Har option ki layout dekho: koi 2 × 2 block hai? koi 5 squares ki row hai?
Quick rules: 2 × 2 block ho toh fail (cube ke corner par sirf 3 faces milte hain, 4 nahi); 5+ squares ek row mein bhi fail. 1-4-1 aur 3-3 staircase valid nets hain.
Cross shape (beech mein 4 ki row, upar-neeche ek-ek square) standard 1-4-1 net hai — valid, cut. Baaki arrangements mein 2 × 2 block dhoondo; trap: sochna ki har net mein 4 ki row zaroori hai.
ga-spatial-15: Tum mirror image dekh rahe ho — 4:37 asli time nahi hai. Vertical mirror left-right ulta karta hai, toh actual aur mirror time ka ek fixed relation hota hai.
Rule: mirror time + actual time = 12:00. Toh actual $= 12{:}00 - 4{:}37$; subtraction ke liye 12:00 ko 11:60 likho.
11:60 se 4:37 column-wise ghatao — minutes alag, hours alag. Trap: borrow bhool ke hour ko 12 se ghata dena, ya 11:59 ko reference le lena.
